headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make Aider↔Cline prompt injection, data leakage, and git-state conflicts plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a git repo; Cline shares state via the filesystem and can use MCP. That creates a default content bridge where one agent can ingest the other's outputs as trusted file content. No provenance or isolation is described, so injection is plausible, though not as direct as a raw shared chat channel.
conditions: IF Aider writes attacker-controlled instructions into repo files that Cline later reads as task context
IF Cline writes prompt-like content into workspace files that Aider then parses as code or guidance
mitigations: Use separate repos/workspaces for the two agents
Add a human review step before either agent consumes the other's output files
Restrict Cline MCP servers to read-only during cross-agent runs
Prefix inter-agent handoff files with a fixed schema and ignore free-form text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and has broad network egress; Cline touches source code and browser screenshots, also with broad egress and MCP access. If they share a repo/workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can flow into either agent's model backend or external tools by default. The blast radius is multiple work products and potentially secrets in the repo.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF either agent sends file contents or screenshots to its configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Disable browser screenshots for Cline when handling secrets
Limit both agents to least-privilege model providers and MCP servers
Rotate or redact secrets before shared-agent sessions
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shells, and use broad network egress. Aider explicitly shares state via a shared git repo, while Cline shares state via the filesystem. Without locking, concurrent edits and git operations can overwrite each other or corrupt history. This matches the high-risk overlap indicator for unrestricted shared writes.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same files in the same repo or workspace
IF both agents perform git commits, rebases, or resets without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time per repo
Use separate branches for each agent
Require manual merge review after each agent's turn
Freeze git operations while the other agent is active
requires-engineering: add file- and git-lock coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider and Cline both act as coding agents that can produce code, patches, and plans. If one agent's output is handed to the other as authoritative task context, the second may propagate mistakes into edits or tool actions. Cline's approval-per-tool helps, but Aider's auto-commit workflow still makes unverified handoffs risky in default pair usage.
conditions: IF Aider-generated patches or explanations are fed into Cline without verification
IF Cline-generated plans are committed or applied by Aider as if they were validated facts
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require tests or lint checks before accepting either agent's output
Use a checklist that separates facts from proposed edits
Keep one agent in read-only review mode
requires-engineering: add structured handoff formats with validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source coding tools with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented in the profiles. The only compliance-relevant difference is that Cline uses browser screenshots and MCP, while Aider uses git history and model-provider APIs. Without a stated regulated-data flow, the pairwise compliance risk is limited and not provably a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into either agent without a matching policy
IF browser screenshots or git history contain data subject to stricter retention rules than the configured provider
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared coding sessions
Disable screenshot capture when not needed
Review provider retention settings before use
Keep separate projects for regulated and unregulated work
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
